name: C compiler in Clojure
mission: A C compiler written in Clojure that compiles real programs (Lua, SQLite) correctly, compiles them fast and generates code that runs as fast as gcc -O2's.
measure: geometric mean, over the hidden SQLite workloads, of instructions executed (callgrind) against gcc -O2's build; every correctness gate must pass (referee/README.md)

lines.title: B8: a C compiler in Clojure, waves W1-W7 (the compiler's origin: arm V)
B9: compile fast (the start of B10: arm V)
B10: an optimising compiler (arm O, the org)

baseline: B8-B10 ran one strong agent (V); it is kept as an arm: V won on cost twice, the org won on correctness (B10's hidden gate)

referee.heldOut: hidden W1-W5 tests and SQLite workloads, held by Meta (referees/)

stopRule: work over 2× its cost target pauses for the owner (PRINCIPLES.md P8)
parkedReason: PRINCIPLES.md P7 (B13: 8 members cost $128 a point against 4 members' $55); kept members by kept credit and points per dollar; see docs/decisions/2026-10-25-principles.md
